title: BIRD: A Trustworthy Bayesian Inference Framework for Large Language Models
abstract: Predictive models often need to work with incomplete information in real-world tasks. Consequently, they must provide reliable probability or confidence estimation, especially in large-scale decision-making and planning tasks. Current large language models (LLMs) are insufficient for accurate estimations, but they can generate relevant factors that may affect the probabilities, produce coarse-grained probabilities when the information is more complete, and help determine which factors are relevant to specific downstream contexts. In this paper, we make use of these capabilities of LLMs to provide a significantly more accurate probabilistic estimation. We propose BIRD, a novel probabilistic inference framework that aligns a Bayesian network with LLM abductions and then estimates more accurate probabilities in a deduction step. We show BIRD provides reliable probability estimations that are 30% better than those provided directly by LLM baselines. These estimates further contribute to better and more trustworthy decision making.

claims.text: BIRD provides estimated outcome probabilities that achieve an F1 score of 59% in human preference alignment on Common2Sense, outperforming direct LLM estimations.
Decision-making via argmax over BIRD predicted probabilities outperforms Chain-of-Thought prompting with Llama-3.1-70B across TODAY, PLASMA, and Common2Sense reasoning benchmarks.
Fine-tuning smaller models using BIRD-estimated soft probabilities as supervision signals improves average cross-domain task accuracy compared to hard label supervision.
Follow-up questions generated by BIRD targeting unobserved Bayesian network factors are preferred by human evaluators over questions generated directly by LLMs.
BIRD constructs a Bayesian network using LLM-generated factors and optimizes its conditional probability table using gradient descent on LLM coarse predictions.

limitations.text: LLMs tend to be inaccurate and overconfident when directly estimating numerical confidences and probabilities.
Standard LLMs cannot provide an out-of-the-box interpretable and controllable process for how their probability estimates are derived.
BIRD assumes that real-world factors are conditionally independent given the context.
BIRD outputs an 'unknown' status when downstream conditions cannot be mapped to any generated Bayesian network factor values.

future_work.text: Applying BIRD in an interactive agent system for more efficient and controlled decision making.

methodologies.name: BIRD (Bayesian Inference from Abduction and Deduction)
methodologies.description: A probabilistic inference framework that aligns a Bayesian network with LLM abductive factor generation, optimizes its conditional probabilities against coarse LLM estimates, and computes outcome probabilities via entailment mapping.
